notes: Policy execution is not a decision: benefits, basic income, job-guarantee wages, upkeep and builds are paid as the player's levers say, so the government chooses only how to fund them, how to cut them pro rata and how its legitimacy moves (known-issues DP-10).
Tax collection and debt service are mechanics, not choices.
The estate pays the pilot in full each month, or what it holds up to the wage. That is accounting, not a choice, so it is not a registered decision (known-issues DP-11).

A flight adds its tonnes (estate.flight_tonnes) to emissions and the estate pays the carbon price (after lobbying) on them; the pilot's wage moves from the estate to the pilot's household. Both are accounting.

Nature is not an agent. It responds to cumulative emissions, the forest stock, commons use and the access rule, and to harvest and fire; only the enclosure of the commons is a registered decision. See the Forest and commons topic for growth and the sink.
Who encloses the commons is matched in the simulation (the richest capital-owning household), not decided here (known-issues DP-11).
Nothing is decided here: each capital-owning household's gift is a decision listed under Households. Here that money becomes pressure on policy levers, held back by union strength.
Nothing is decided here: the odds follow climate stress, dryness and fire station coverage, and the outcome is a random draw.

net_signs.label: Pushes it up
net_signs.text: When this goes up, the quantity goes up, along every route of at most three steps.

net_signs.label: Pushes it down
net_signs.text: When this goes up, the quantity goes down, along every route of at most three steps.

net_signs.label: Depends
net_signs.text: Some link on the way can push either way depending on the state of the town, so the overall push is not fixed.

net_signs.label: Both ways
net_signs.text: Different routes push in opposite directions: it raises the quantity along one route and lowers it along another, so no single sign is given.

net_signs.label: No direct push
net_signs.text: The quantity reads this, but no route of signed links carries a change of it to the quantity.

roles.label: Starting point
roles.text: Nothing in the registry writes it: a state variable, a lever or a setting the chain starts from, or something whose cause is not described yet.

roles.label: In the middle
roles.text: A decision or a piece of plain code writes it and another one reads it.

roles.label: End point
roles.text: Written by a decision or a piece of plain code, but nothing else reads it: an outcome.

roles.label: Decision
roles.text: A choice that reads some quantities and writes others.

roles.label: Mechanism
roles.text: Plain physics or accounting that nobody chooses (production, emissions, weather, rent, taxes): it reads some quantities and writes others by a fixed rule.

aggregates.label: Town figure
aggregates.text: One number for the whole town.

aggregates.label: Total
aggregates.text: Added up over the active firms or over all households.

aggregates.label: Average
aggregates.text: The average over the active firms.

aggregates.label: Setting
aggregates.text: The setting of a policy lever now (the effective one where lobbying can change it).

aggregates.label: Yes or no
aggregates.text: Shown as 1 for yes and 0 for no.

unbound.label: Inside one agent
unbound.text: A working variable of a single firm, household or bank. The town has no one number for it.

unbound.label: Worked out each month
unbound.text: A rule computes it fresh every month and does not keep it, so there is no stored value to show.

unbound.label: Not shown yet
unbound.text: It exists in the simulation, but the game does not publish a town figure for it yet.

unbound.label: A fixed setting
unbound.text: A fixed setting of the model's rules rather than a number that moves.

unbound.label: Chance
unbound.text: A random draw, different every time, with no value to track.

effects.varies: when {input} goes up, {output} can go up or down: {reason}
effects.none: {input} is read here but does not directly change {output}: {reason}.

basis.perturbed: Checked by raising the input in the real code and measuring the output.
basis.system: Checked by raising the input in a real game state, running the real system and measuring the output.
basis.declared_unverified: Declared from the code and economics, not measured: {reason}

because_overrides.because: wages are most of what it costs to make a unit
the carbon charge is part of the cost of every unit
the same wage bill is spread over more units
better weather lets each worker make more, so fewer are needed for the same output
more expected sales need more output, so more workers
when many people are jobless, firms can hold wages down
a higher harvest lever makes each unit of food take more of the commons, so the commons run out sooner
served is the share of demand the plants can meet, and a bigger demand spreads the same supply thinner
stress grows as the carbon budget is used up
the tax is the rate times the wages paid
a firm with more debt for its assets is riskier, so the bank charges more
people blame the government for joblessness
a household cannot spend more than it has saved
when every home is taken, landlords can raise the rent
a higher carbon price makes cutting emissions pay back sooner

kinds.label: Reinforcing
kinds.text: Each trip round the loop pushes the change further the same way, so it snowballs (growth, or collapse) until something else stops it.

kinds.label: Balancing
kinds.text: Each trip round the loop pushes the change back, so the loop steadies things (and can overshoot when it is slow).

kinds.label: Depends
kinds.text: At least one link in this loop can push either way depending on the state of the town, so it is not called reinforcing or balancing.

loops.delay_one: About 1 month to come round the loop.
loops.delay_many: About {n} months to come round the loop.

incomplete.label: Includes a policy setting
incomplete.text: One of its links is a policy setting, which the player moves, so the loop is only part of the story.

incomplete.label: Partly modelled
incomplete.text: One of its quantities is also changed by plain code the registry does not describe (docs/known-issues.md DP-13), so the loop may be missing a link.

incomplete.label: A link is not measured
incomplete.text: One of its links has a sign that is declared from the code and reasoning but could not be measured (docs/known-issues.md DP-18).

names.name: Growth
names.story: Profit pays for investment, investment builds capital, capital raises output, and what is made and sold earns the next profit. It also drives emissions up.

names.name: Wage bill squeezes payouts
names.story: Hiring raises the wage bill, which leaves less profit to pay out as dividends, so households save and spend less; demand and expected sales fall, and with them hiring.

names.name: Reserve army
names.story: Unemployment holds wages down, lower wages cut the firm's unit cost and price, a cheaper price lifts demand and hiring, and hiring lowers unemployment.

names.name: Tragedy of the commons
names.story: Farm output draws on the commons, and a smaller commons caps what the farm can make.

names.name: Overshoot bites
names.story: Output makes emissions, emissions use up the carbon budget and raise climate stress and drought, and drought cuts output. The damage slows the thing that causes it.

names.name: Dying forests
names.story: Emissions raise climate stress and fire risk, fire burns the forest, a smaller forest takes in less carbon, so emissions build up faster.

names.name: Green investment
names.story: A firm's footprint makes green technology pay, and green technology lowers the footprint. The carbon price (a policy setting) feeds green technology from outside the loop.

quantities.label: Expected sales
quantities.summary: A smoothed average of past demand for what the firm makes.

quantities.label: Inventory
quantities.summary: Unsold stock the firm holds.

quantities.label: Inventory cover wanted
quantities.summary: How many months of sales the firm likes to hold as stock (services cannot be stored, so they hold none).

quantities.label: Workers
quantities.summary: The people the firm employs.

quantities.label: Skilled workers
quantities.summary: Workers whose skill is at or above the skilled threshold.

quantities.label: Effective labour per worker
quantities.summary: What an average worker contributes after skill and commute time.

quantities.label: Output from capital and technology
quantities.summary: What one unit of labour would make with the firm's capital and technology, before weather, resources and the transition take their share.

quantities.label: Weather and climate effect on output
quantities.summary: Climate damage, drought and smoke from nearby fires, which cut what a firm can make (climate damage and drought hit farms only).

quantities.label: Natural resources effect on output
quantities.summary: The health of the forest and commons a farm relies on, and the coordination cost of a community-managed commons.

quantities.label: Transition effect on output
quantities.summary: Output lost while the town changes its economic system.

quantities.label: Workers wanted
quantities.summary: The headcount that would produce the output the firm wants.

quantities.label: Vacancies
quantities.summary: Jobs the firm posts this month, skilled and general.

quantities.label: Months overstaffed
quantities.summary: How many months in a row the firm has had more workers than it wants.

quantities.label: Unemployment
quantities.summary: The town's smoothed unemployment rate, which firms watch when they set wages.

quantities.label: Base wage
quantities.summary: The firm's base monthly wage.

quantities.label: Minimum wage
quantities.summary: The legal wage floor (the player's lever).

quantities.label: Sector productivity growth
quantities.summary: How fast output per worker grows in the firm's sector; wages follow it so that wages and prices do not drift apart.

quantities.label: Price
quantities.summary: What the firm charges for one unit.

quantities.label: Markup
quantities.summary: The margin over unit cost the firm aims for. It is the firm's own state, set at the start and copied to a new firm, not a parameter.

quantities.label: Unit cost
quantities.summary: Wages plus carbon cost for each unit made.

quantities.label: Carbon footprint
quantities.summary: Direct emissions plus the emissions of the electricity the firm uses.

quantities.label: Carbon price firms plan with
quantities.summary: The carbon price in force after lobbying, pulled toward a price the player has announced but not yet started.

quantities.label: Revenue
quantities.summary: What the firm earned selling this month.

quantities.label: Emissions cap
quantities.summary: The cap in force after lobbying (0 means no cap).

quantities.label: Green subsidy
quantities.summary: The share of a green investment the treasury pays.

quantities.label: Treasury cash
quantities.summary: Cash the government holds; it limits the subsidies it can pay.

quantities.label: Cash
quantities.summary: Cash the firm holds when it decides.

quantities.label: Cash reserve
quantities.summary: Cash kept back for payroll and debt service.

quantities.label: Green technology
quantities.summary: How much of its emissions the firm has cut with clean technology.

quantities.label: Saving for green investment
quantities.summary: The firm wants a green step but cannot afford it yet, so it holds cash back.

quantities.label: Profit
quantities.summary: Profit after interest, carbon cost and tax this month.

quantities.label: Profit trend
quantities.summary: A smoothed average of past profit.

quantities.label: Capital
quantities.summary: The firm's capital stock after depreciation and this month's purchases.

quantities.label: Capital needed per unit sold
quantities.summary: How much capital the firm's technology needs for each unit of expected sales.

quantities.label: Loan rate
quantities.summary: The interest rate the bank charges the firm.

quantities.label: In distress
quantities.summary: The firm has been behind on payments or could not pay wages in full.

quantities.label: Required return above the loan rate
quantities.summary: How much more than the loan rate an investment must earn; set by the economic system.

quantities.label: Cash held for green investment
quantities.summary: The share of free cash held back while a green step is planned; set by the economic system.

quantities.label: Planned investment
quantities.summary: What the firm plans to spend on capital goods next month.

quantities.label: Loan request
quantities.summary: What the firm asks the bank to lend for its plan.

quantities.label: Wages paid
quantities.summary: What the firm paid its workers this month.

quantities.label: Debt service due
quantities.summary: Interest plus scheduled principal due this month.

quantities.label: Payout ratio
quantities.summary: The share of profit paid out; set by the economic system.

quantities.label: Dividends
quantities.summary: What the firm pays its owners this month.

quantities.label: Debt
quantities.summary: What the firm owes the bank.

quantities.label: Missed payments
quantities.summary: Interest, scheduled principal or wages went unpaid this month.

quantities.label: Months in distress
quantities.summary: How many months in a row the firm has missed payments.

quantities.label: Firm open
quantities.summary: Whether the firm keeps trading or defaults and closes.

quantities.label: Sector return
quantities.summary: The average return on capital in a sector that has room for another firm.

quantities.label: Cost of borrowing
quantities.summary: The base rate plus the bank's base spread.

quantities.label: Random draw
quantities.summary: A chance draw the simulation takes each month and hands to the decision.

quantities.label: New firm
quantities.summary: A household founds a firm in the dormant slot.

quantities.label: Savings
quantities.summary: The deposits a household holds.

quantities.label: Last month's disposable income
quantities.summary: Income after tax, rent and loan payments last month.

quantities.label: Net wealth
quantities.summary: Savings, homes and firm shares owned, less debt.

quantities.label: Food price
quantities.summary: The average price of food across the food firms.

quantities.label: Food need
quantities.summary: The food a household needs each month: a fixed amount per person.

quantities.label: Household size
quantities.summary: How many people live in the household.

quantities.label: Spending propensity
quantities.summary: The share of spare income a household of this class spends rather than saves.

quantities.label: Spending out of wealth
quantities.unit: share of net wealth per month
quantities.summary: The slice of net wealth the owner classes also spend each month (zero for other classes).

quantities.label: Spending budget
quantities.summary: The money a buyer brings to a market: households split theirs into food, goods and services; firms and the government buy in the same markets.

quantities.label: Demand
quantities.summary: What buyers wanted from the firm this month, in units, even if its stock ran out.

quantities.label: Units sold
quantities.summary: What the firm actually sold this month.

quantities.label: Capital income
quantities.summary: Dividends, rent and interest a household received last month.

quantities.label: Campaign spending cap
quantities.summary: The player-set limit on the share of income that may go to lobbying.

quantities.label: Lobbying spend
quantities.summary: What a capital-owning household gives to lobbying this month.

quantities.label: Bank equity
quantities.summary: The bank's own money: what its loans are worth less what it owes depositors.

quantities.label: Bank loans
quantities.summary: All the loans the bank has made.

quantities.label: Bank deposits
quantities.summary: What the bank owes its depositors.

quantities.label: Required capital ratio
quantities.summary: The player-set minimum of equity to loans.

quantities.label: Lending room
quantities.summary: How much more the bank may lend before it breaks the capital ratio.

quantities.label: Firm assets
quantities.summary: What a firm owns: capital at its price plus cash.

quantities.label: Loan approved
quantities.summary: What the bank agrees to lend the firm this month.

quantities.label: System credit spread
quantities.summary: Extra interest the economic system adds on top of the usual spread.

quantities.label: Bank dividend
quantities.summary: Equity above the required buffer that the bank pays to its owner.

quantities.label: Policy rate
quantities.summary: The base interest rate the player sets.

quantities.label: Bailout policy
quantities.summary: Whether the treasury recapitalises a failing bank.

quantities.label: Bank failed
quantities.summary: The bank is out of equity and has no bailout: depositors lose part of their savings.

quantities.label: Committed spending
quantities.summary: What the government owes this month: benefits, UBI, job-guarantee wages, upkeep and building.

quantities.label: Next month's purchases
quantities.summary: The goods the government plans to buy next month (the spending lever), held back in cash.

quantities.label: Taxes collected
quantities.summary: Taxes and carbon payments that came in this month.

quantities.label: Public debt
quantities.summary: What the government owes the bank.

quantities.label: Borrowing
quantities.summary: New loans the government takes from the bank this month.

quantities.label: Repayment
quantities.summary: Debt the government pays back this month.

quantities.label: Share of spending paid
quantities.summary: The share of each committed payment the treasury can actually fund (1 means all of it).

quantities.label: Legitimacy
quantities.summary: How far the town accepts the government's rule; it drifts with wellbeing, unemployment, inequality, debt, bailouts and system change.

quantities.label: Wellbeing
quantities.summary: The town's average wellbeing.

quantities.label: Inequality
quantities.summary: The Gini coefficient of household wealth.

quantities.label: Public debt against GDP
quantities.summary: Public debt divided by a year's GDP.

quantities.label: Bank bailed out
quantities.summary: Whether the treasury rescued the bank this month.

quantities.label: Resistance to system change
quantities.summary: The legitimacy lost each month while the town changes its economic system.

quantities.label: Pilot on the payroll
quantities.summary: Whether the jet's pilot works for the estate right now (true also when the town has no pilot to need).

quantities.label: Months of short pay
quantities.summary: How many months in a row the estate could not pay the pilot in full.

quantities.label: Pilot free to rehire
quantities.summary: The pilot has no other job and is not on the job guarantee.

quantities.label: Estate savings
quantities.summary: The deposits the estate household holds.

quantities.label: Jet flies
quantities.summary: Whether the jet flies this month.

quantities.label: Chance of enclosure
quantities.summary: The chance each month that a wealthy owner fences off an open commons; it depends on the economic system.

quantities.label: Commons open
quantities.summary: Whether anyone may use the commons (not enclosed and not community-managed).

quantities.label: Commons enclosed
quantities.summary: Whether an owner has fenced the commons off.

quantities.label: Forest
quantities.summary: How much forest is left, as a share of the most the land can hold. It absorbs carbon, helps the farm and is cleared when the town builds.

quantities.label: Commons
quantities.summary: How much of the shared grazing and fishing land is left, as a share of the most it can hold. It regrows slowly and the farm takes food from it.

quantities.label: Commons run by the community
quantities.summary: Whether the commons are managed by the community, which caps what the farm may take and cushions droughts at a small coordination cost.

quantities.label: Commons harvest setting
quantities.summary: The policy lever for how much of the usual harvest the farm may take from the commons.

quantities.label: Net emissions so far
quantities.summary: All the carbon the town has emitted so far, less what the forest absorbed. It is the number the 1.5 C carbon budget is measured against.

quantities.label: Emissions per month (before the forest)
quantities.summary: Everything the town emits in a month: firms, power plants, households and any private flight.

quantities.label: Carbon the forest absorbs
quantities.summary: The carbon the forest takes out of the air each month, in proportion to how much forest there is.

quantities.label: Net emissions per month
quantities.summary: Gross emissions less what the forest absorbs. It adds to the carbon already emitted.

quantities.label: Firms' direct emissions
quantities.summary: The carbon firms emit making their goods, before counting the electricity they use.

quantities.label: Power plants' emissions
quantities.summary: The carbon fossil power plants emit making the electricity the town uses. Renewable plants emit none.

quantities.label: Carbon per unit of electricity
quantities.summary: How much carbon one unit of electricity carries: higher when more of the plants burn fossil fuel.

quantities.label: Renewable share of the plants
quantities.summary: The share of the town's power capacity that is renewable rather than fossil.

quantities.label: Power plant capacity
quantities.summary: The most electricity all the plants together can supply in a month.

quantities.label: Electricity demanded
quantities.summary: The electricity firms and households would like to use this month, before any rationing.

quantities.label: Share of electricity delivered
quantities.summary: The share of what firms and households asked for that the plants can deliver. Below 1 means rationing, and firms make less.

quantities.label: Climate stress
quantities.summary: How hard the climate is pressing: 0 while the carbon budget is healthy, 1 when it has run out. It raises the odds of droughts and fires.

quantities.label: Drought under way
quantities.summary: Whether a drought is on. It cuts farm output and commons regrowth and raises electricity use.

quantities.label: Fire burning
quantities.summary: Whether a forest fire is burning. It burns forest, smokes out nearby firms and makes people unhappy.

quantities.label: Resilience spending
quantities.summary: The policy lever for spending on defences against drought and fire.

quantities.label: Economic system change under way
quantities.summary: Whether the town is switching economic system. Output dips while it happens.

quantities.label: Output
quantities.summary: What the firms actually make in a month, after electricity rationing, the emissions cap and nature's limits.

quantities.label: Technology
quantities.summary: How much a firm gets out of its capital and labour. It creeps up a little each month.

quantities.label: Household spending
quantities.summary: What a household actually spent last month on goods and food.

quantities.label: Private rent
quantities.summary: The rent for a privately owned home. It rises while every home is taken and falls otherwise.

quantities.label: Homes occupied
quantities.summary: The share of homes that have a household living in them.

quantities.label: Profit tax rate
quantities.summary: The policy lever for the tax on firm profit (the rate in force, after lobbying).

quantities.label: Wage tax rate
quantities.summary: The policy lever for the tax on wages.

quantities.label: Capital income tax rate
quantities.summary: The policy lever for the tax on dividends and rent.

quantities.label: Wealth tax rate
quantities.summary: The policy lever for the tax on wealth above the threshold (the rate in force, after lobbying).

quantities.label: Wealth tax threshold
quantities.summary: The policy lever for how much wealth a household may hold before the wealth tax applies.

decisions.title: Hire
decisions.decides: How many workers to want and how many jobs to post (hiring up to a monthly cap)

rule.label: Size the workforce to expected sales and stock
rule.text: Needed output = expected sales x (1 + growth aspiration) + inventory adjust x (cover x expected sales - inventory). Workers wanted = labour that output needs, in people. It posts vacancies once the gap exceeds the hiring slack, and the skilled tier gets what it is short of.

decisions.title: Fire
decisions.decides: Whether to let people go: only after a sustained surplus of workers, the least skilled first

rule.label: Fire after months of surplus
rule.text: Each month the firm is overstaffed by at least the firing slack it counts one more month. After enough months in a row it lets go up to a monthly cap, and the count resets.

decisions.title: Wage
decisions.decides: The base wage, adjusted each month

rule.label: Productivity trend plus a response to slack
rule.text: Wage step = trend + wage_k x (reference unemployment - unemployment), capped each month, where the trend is the expected inflation plus the sector's productivity growth. The wage never falls below the legal minimum.

decisions.title: Price
decisions.decides: The price it charges, adjusted each month

rule.label: Move toward unit cost plus a markup
rule.text: Price moves a share (price adjust) of the way toward (1 + markup) x unit cost each month, never below the minimum price. Demand never enters: excess demand shows up in hiring, not in the price.

decisions.title: Green technology
decisions.decides: Whether to buy a step of clean technology this month, and whether to save for one

rule.label: Buy when the carbon bill over the payback period beats the cost
rule.text: A step is worthwhile when the carbon bill over the payback period is larger than its cost, or an emissions cap binds, and the firm is below the technology ceiling. The firm buys it if its cash above the reserve covers its share after any subsidy; otherwise it holds cash back for it.

decisions.title: Investment and borrowing
decisions.decides: How much capital to buy next month and how much to borrow for it

rule.label: Replace capital and grow toward expected sales, if the return beats the loan rate
rule.text: Planned capital = depreciation + accelerator x (capital that expected sales call for - capital), scaled by a gate that is high when the smoothed return beats the loan rate plus the hurdle, and capped. It pays part from free cash and asks the bank for the rest. A firm in distress plans nothing.

decisions.title: Dividends
decisions.decides: How much to pay its owners

rule.label: Pay a share of profit, never below the cash reserve
rule.text: Regular dividend = payout ratio x profit, but only out of cash above the reserve for payroll and debt service. Idle cash well above that is also paid out at a set rate.

decisions.title: Closing down
decisions.decides: Whether to default and close

rule.label: Default after months of missed payments
rule.text: Each month the firm misses interest, principal or wages it counts one more month in distress; a clean month resets the count. After enough months in a row, if it still owes money, it defaults and closes.

decisions.title: Founding a firm
decisions.decides: Whether to found a firm in the dormant slot

rule.label: A chance that grows with the return over the cost of borrowing
rule.text: Which household can found (a Worker or Manager with enough savings) and which slot are matched first. The chance this month = mobility rate x (sector return - cost of borrowing), between 0 and 1; the firm is founded if the month's random draw falls below it.

decisions.title: Spending
decisions.decides: How much to spend on food, goods and services this month

rule.label: Food first, then a share of what is left
rule.text: Food need = people x food per person; the household buys that first, up to its savings. Of what is left of last month's disposable income it spends its class's propensity; the owner classes also spend a small slice of net wealth. The total cannot exceed savings, and is split into goods and services.

decisions.title: Shopping
decisions.decides: Which firm in each market gets the money

rule.label: Cheaper firms with more stock get more
rule.text: Each firm's weight = its stock x (average price / its price) ^ elasticity. The budget is shared in proportion to weight, in two passes so a firm cannot sell more than it holds. What buyers wanted at their share, even beyond stock, is its demand. Firms buying capital goods and the government use the same split.

decisions.title: Expecting sales
decisions.decides: What sales to expect next month

rule.label: A smoothing of demand
rule.text: Expected sales = weight x this month's demand + (1 - weight) x last expectation. Hiring and production read it, so spending reaches jobs here.

decisions.title: Lobbying
decisions.decides: How much a capital-owning household gives to lobbying

rule.label: A share of capital income, within savings and the cap
rule.text: Spend = capital income x the smaller of the spend rate and the campaign cap, never more than savings. Which households lobby (Capitalists and Rentiers) and who receives the money are matched first.

decisions.title: Lending room
decisions.decides: How much more the bank may lend

rule.label: Equity divided by the required ratio
rule.text: Most the bank may have lent = equity / required capital ratio (nothing if the ratio is zero). Room = that less its loans, never below zero.

decisions.title: Lending
decisions.decides: How much to lend each firm that asks

rule.label: The request, within the bank's room and the firm's leverage cap
rule.text: Approved = the smallest of the request, the bank's remaining room, and (maximum leverage x firm assets - its debt), never below zero. Firms are served in order until the room is used up.

decisions.title: Interest rate
decisions.decides: The interest rate each firm pays

rule.label: Base rate plus a spread that grows with leverage
rule.text: Rate = policy rate + base spread + leverage spread x (debt / assets) + any extra spread the economic system adds. Riskier, more indebted firms pay more.

decisions.title: Bank payout
decisions.decides: How much of its excess capital the bank pays out

rule.label: Pay out part of equity above a buffer
rule.text: Required = loans x capital ratio x (1 + buffer). Excess = equity - required (never below zero). It pays out the payout share of the excess to its owner.

decisions.title: Rescue or failure
decisions.decides: What happens when the bank's equity goes negative

rule.label: The treasury recapitalises it, or depositors take a loss
rule.text: If equity is negative and the bailout policy is on, new money restores equity to the target share of loans. Without it the bank fails and every deposit loses a share: the shortfall over deposits, plus a margin.

decisions.title: Funding the month
decisions.decides: How to fund the month's payments: borrow the gap, or repay debt

rule.label: Cash and taxes first, then the bank, within its lending room
rule.text: The treasury needs this month's committed payments plus next month's planned purchases. If cash and taxes fall short, it borrows the gap, up to the bank's lending room. If they cover it, it repays a share of the surplus, up to what it owes.

decisions.title: Cutting spending
decisions.decides: How much of its payments to cut when the treasury runs short

rule.label: Every payment is cut by the same share
rule.text: If cash, taxes and borrowing cannot cover the committed payments, each payment is paid at the same share (funds over commitments) and the shortfall is reported. Otherwise everything is paid in full.

decisions.title: Legitimacy
decisions.decides: How its legitimacy moves each month

rule.label: Drifts with wellbeing, unemployment, inequality, debt, bailouts and system change
rule.text: Legitimacy changes by a wellbeing weight x (wellbeing - neutral), less a weight x the amount unemployment and the Gini exceed their thresholds, less a weight x the amount public debt exceeds a year's GDP, less a penalty if the bank was bailed out, less the resistance to a system change under way. It stays between 0 and 1.

decisions.title: Keeping the pilot
decisions.decides: Whether to let the pilot go, or hire the pilot back

rule.label: Let go after months of short pay, hired back once savings cover wages
rule.text: If the pilot is employed and has gone unpaid in full for the maximum number of months in a row, the pilot is let go. If not employed, with no other job, and the estate's savings cover the set months of wages, the pilot is hired back.

decisions.title: Flying the jet
decisions.decides: Whether the jet flies this month

rule.label: A monthly chance, and only with a pilot
rule.text: The simulation takes one random draw each month. The jet flies if the draw falls below the monthly chance and a pilot is on the payroll (or the town has no pilot).

decisions.title: Fencing off the commons
decisions.decides: Whether an owner fences off an open commons this month

rule.label: A monthly chance while the commons are open
rule.text: While the commons are open, each month's random draw is compared with the economic system's chance of enclosure; below it, the richest capital-owning household fences the commons off. Who that is, is matched in the simulation.

mechanisms.title: Technology, capital and labour make output
mechanisms.explains: Output before the factors below is technology times capital to a power times labour to a power.

rule.label: Cobb-Douglas production
rule.text: Output = technology x capital^a x labour^b, with a = 0.3 and b = 0.7 here: more capital or more labour make more output, with diminishing returns.

mechanisms.title: Technology creeps up
mechanisms.explains: A firm's technology grows a little every month, at a rate set by its sector.

rule.label: Steady technological drift
rule.text: Technology next month = technology x (1 + the sector's growth rate). Nothing a firm decides changes it.

mechanisms.title: Capital wears out and is added to
mechanisms.explains: Capital loses a share each month, and last month's investment is added; building clears a little forest.

rule.label: Depreciate, then add investment
rule.text: Capital next month = capital x (1 - depreciation) + the money planned for investment / the price of a unit of capital. Each dollar built also clears some forest.

mechanisms.title: Workers supply effective labour
mechanisms.explains: A firm's labour is its workers' skill times the hours they work.

rule.label: Skill times hours
rule.text: Effective labour = the sum over the firm's workers of skill x effective hours. Skilled workers and longer working hours count for more.

mechanisms.title: The farm needs healthy forest and commons
mechanisms.explains: The farm's output is scaled by the health of the forest and the commons.

rule.label: Output follows resource health
rule.text: Farm output is multiplied by (the average of forest health and commons health) to a power, so a depleted forest or commons cuts food. A community-managed commons costs a little output in coordination.

mechanisms.title: Climate damage cuts farm output
mechanisms.explains: The farm loses a share of its output that grows with the carbon emitted so far.

rule.label: Damage grows with the square of the budget used
rule.text: Share lost = damage x (emissions so far / carbon budget)^2, with the ratio capped. It is the slow cost of the carbon already in the air.

mechanisms.title: Drought cuts farm output
mechanisms.explains: While a drought lasts the farm loses output; resilience spending softens it.

rule.label: Drought loss, softened by resilience
rule.text: Output is multiplied by 1 - a x (drought severity, cut by resilience spending). Resilience spending protects up to a ceiling.

mechanisms.title: Smoke cuts output near a fire
mechanisms.explains: Every firm near a burning tile loses a little output.

rule.label: Smoke loss
rule.text: Output is multiplied by 1 - the smoke loss for any firm within the smoke radius of a fire.

mechanisms.title: A change of system costs output
mechanisms.explains: While the economic system changes, every firm makes less.

rule.label: Transition output penalty
rule.text: Output is multiplied by 1 - the penalty set in the system file, for as long as the switch takes. (The penalty is a setting of the system files, not of params.json.)

mechanisms.title: Output: capacity, rationing and the cap
mechanisms.explains: Output is the capacity the factors give, cut by electricity rationing and by the emissions cap.

rule.label: Capacity, then rationing, then the cap
rule.text: Capacity = production x farm health x climate x drought x smoke x transition. It is then multiplied by the share of electricity delivered, and cannot exceed the emissions cap divided by the firm's carbon per unit.

mechanisms.title: Nature limits how much food can grow
mechanisms.explains: The food the farms can grow is capped by what the forest and the commons can supply.

rule.label: Food limited by stocks
rule.text: Food cannot exceed the tighter of two caps: the commons supply (a share of the stock, limited by who controls access) over the commons taken per unit of food, and the same for the forest.

mechanisms.title: Stock carries over and this month's output is added
mechanisms.explains: What a firm did not sell loses a little to holding costs, and this month's output is added.

rule.label: Stock decay plus output
rule.text: Stock next month = stock x (1 - holding cost) + this month's output. Services cannot be stored: their holding cost is 100 per cent.

mechanisms.title: Firms and households need electricity
mechanisms.explains: Firms need electricity per unit made and households per person and per dollar spent; a drought raises both.

rule.label: Electricity per unit and per person
rule.text: Firm demand = planned output x electricity per unit (cut by green technology) x a heat factor. Household demand = people x (base + extra for each dollar spent). A drought raises both.

mechanisms.title: Plants deliver what they can
mechanisms.explains: The share of electricity delivered is what the plants can supply over what is asked, at most 1.

rule.label: Served share
rule.text: Served = supply / demand when demand exceeds supply, otherwise 1. Below the rationing threshold the town is told electricity is rationed.

mechanisms.title: The mix of plants sets carbon per unit of electricity
mechanisms.explains: Carbon per unit of electricity is the fossil share of capacity times the fossil factor.

rule.label: Fossil share times factor
rule.text: Grid intensity = (fossil capacity / total capacity) x tonnes of carbon per unit of fossil electricity. Building renewables lowers it.

mechanisms.title: Firms emit in proportion to output
mechanisms.explains: A firm's direct emissions are its output times its carbon intensity, cut by green technology; its footprint adds its electricity.

rule.label: Intensity times output
rule.text: Direct emissions = output x base intensity x (1 - green technology). Footprint = direct emissions + the electricity used x carbon per unit of electricity.

mechanisms.title: Only fossil plants emit
mechanisms.explains: Fossil plants emit in proportion to the electricity they deliver.

rule.label: Fossil plants emit
rule.text: Each plant delivers its capacity share of the electricity used; fossil plants emit that x the fossil factor, renewable plants nothing.

mechanisms.title: Emissions are added up
mechanisms.explains: Gross emissions are firms' direct emissions, plants, households and any private flight, summed.

rule.label: Sum of the sources
rule.text: Gross emissions = firms' direct + plants' + households' (people x direct emissions each) + any flight's tonnes.

mechanisms.title: Net emissions use up the carbon budget
mechanisms.explains: Net emissions are gross emissions less what the forest absorbs, and they add to the carbon emitted so far.

rule.label: Net emissions accumulate
rule.text: Net = gross - forest absorption. Total so far = total so far + net, never below zero. The carbon budget is measured against this total.

mechanisms.title: The forest absorbs carbon
mechanisms.explains: The forest absorbs carbon in proportion to how much of it there is.

rule.label: Absorption per unit of forest
rule.text: Carbon absorbed per month = absorption rate x forest stock. Cutting or burning forest therefore also cuts the sink.

mechanisms.title: The forest regrows and is harvested
mechanisms.explains: The forest regrows along a logistic curve and the farms take some for each unit of food.

rule.label: Logistic growth less harvest
rule.text: Forest next month = forest + growth x forest x (1 - forest / maximum) - the harvest (food made x forest taken per unit) - any clearing for building.

mechanisms.title: The commons regrow and are harvested
mechanisms.explains: The commons regrow along a logistic curve, slowed by drought, and the farms take some; access rules limit the take.

rule.label: Logistic growth less harvest
rule.text: Commons next month = commons + growth x commons x (1 - commons / maximum) x (share surviving drought) - the harvest. A fenced-off commons allows more harvest; a community-managed one is capped and cushions drought.

mechanisms.title: Fire burns forest
mechanisms.explains: Burning tiles lose a share of the forest stock each month.

rule.label: Burn loss
rule.text: Forest lost = burning tiles x burn share x (forest / forest tiles). Burnt tiles then regrow slowly.

mechanisms.title: Emissions raise climate stress
mechanisms.explains: Climate stress is 0 until the carbon budget runs low and rises to 1 as it runs out.

rule.label: Stress from the budget used
rule.text: Stress = ((onset - budget left) / (onset - full)) clamped to 0..1, raised to a curve exponent. It is the one link from emissions to the weather.

mechanisms.title: Stress makes droughts likelier
mechanisms.explains: A drought starts by chance, likelier and more severe as stress rises, and ends when its months run out.

rule.label: Drought chance by stress
rule.text: Monthly chance = base x (1 + gain x stress). Severity and length are drawn from ranges that widen with stress. The draw is random, so two games differ.

mechanisms.title: Dry conditions start and spread fires
mechanisms.explains: Fires start by chance and spread to neighbouring forest tiles, more in dry conditions, less with fire stations and resilience spending.

rule.label: Fire chance by dryness
rule.text: Ignition chance = base x (1 + gain x stress) x dryness x share of forest standing x (1 - resilience cut). Dryness grows with a depleted commons and with drought. Spread chance rises with drought and falls near a fire station.

mechanisms.title: Wellbeing blends what people need
mechanisms.explains: Each person's wellbeing moves toward a weighted blend of consumption, a job, a home, a clean environment, savings, a short commute and clean local air.

rule.label: Weighted blend of needs
rule.text: Target = weighted sum of: spending against needs, having a job, being housed, forest times clean air, savings against a few months of needs, less a long commute, nearby fossil plants and smoke. Wellbeing moves a share of the way to it each month.

mechanisms.title: Inequality is the Gini of wealth
mechanisms.explains: Inequality is how unevenly wealth is spread across people (0 = equal, 1 = one person has all).

rule.label: Gini of wealth
rule.text: The Gini coefficient of each person's wealth (their share of the household's wealth).

mechanisms.title: Last month's income is remembered
mechanisms.explains: A household's disposable income is recorded each month and used to decide next month's spending and moves.

rule.label: Income less taxes and rent
rule.text: Disposable income = wages + capital income + transfers, less taxes and rent paid. It is stored for next month.

mechanisms.title: Firms pay wages
mechanisms.explains: Firms pay each worker their wage, scaled down if the firm's cash falls short; the pay lands in the worker's household.

rule.label: Pay up to the cash in hand
rule.text: Each worker is paid the wage due; if the total due exceeds the firm's cash, everyone is paid the same share of it. Wages paid is the firm's payroll.

mechanisms.title: Dividends and rent reach households
mechanisms.explains: Dividends go to the firm's owners and rent to the home's owner.

rule.label: Dividends and rent received
rule.text: Each month a firm's dividend goes to its owner (a household, the bank's owner, the state or its workers), and renters pay rent to the home's owner. Both add to the receiving household's savings and capital income.

mechanisms.title: Profit is what is left
mechanisms.explains: Profit is revenue less wages, loan interest, the carbon charge and profit tax.

rule.label: Revenue less costs and taxes
rule.text: Profit = revenue - wages paid - interest - carbon charge (carbon price x footprint) - profit tax (rate x the profit before tax).

mechanisms.title: The treasury collects taxes
mechanisms.explains: The government collects taxes on wages, capital income and wealth, and what firms pay in carbon charge and profit tax.

rule.label: Taxes by base and rate
rule.text: Receipts = wage tax x wages + capital tax x capital income + wealth tax x wealth above the threshold + firms' carbon charge + firms' profit tax. Collecting is not a choice; what to do with the money is (see the government's decisions).

mechanisms.title: Purchases move money and stock
mechanisms.explains: What households buy moves money from their savings to the firm, takes units out of its stock and counts as their spending.

rule.label: Units times price
rule.text: Revenue = units sold x price. Stock falls by the units sold; the buyers' savings fall by what they paid and their recorded spending rises by it.

mechanisms.title: Wages and carbon make up a firm's unit cost
mechanisms.explains: A firm's unit cost is its wage bill plus its carbon charge, per unit made.

rule.label: Wages plus carbon per unit
rule.text: Unit cost = (wage bill + carbon charge) / output. The price rule then moves price toward unit cost plus markup, so wages and the carbon price pass into prices.

mechanisms.title: Rent follows occupancy and what renters can bear
mechanisms.explains: Rent rises while every home is taken and renters can bear it, and falls otherwise.

rule.label: Rent follows occupancy and burden
rule.text: If occupancy is at or above the trigger and rent takes less than the burden cap of renters' income, rent rises by a set share; otherwise it falls by one, never below the floor.

mechanisms.title: Households move to what they can afford
mechanisms.explains: Households move to a home whose rent they can afford; unpaid rent for too long loses the home.

rule.label: Move and evict by affordability
rule.text: A household moves to the cheapest free home whose rent is within the share of its income it will pay. After enough months of unpaid rent a tenant is evicted. Both change how many homes are occupied.

mechanisms.title: Vacancies are filled from the jobless
mechanisms.explains: Posted vacancies are filled from people without work, those who ask the least first.

rule.label: Fill vacancies from the jobless
rule.text: Each firm's vacancies are filled from the jobless in the labour force, in order of the pay they ask, up to the firm's monthly hiring cap. Fewer jobless than vacancies leaves jobs open.

mechanisms.title: Unemployment is the jobless share
mechanisms.explains: Unemployment is the share of the labour force without a job.

rule.label: Jobless share of the labour force
rule.text: Unemployment = people in the labour force with no job / people in the labour force.
